You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2008, with a financial crisis in progress: VIX, credit spreads and the dollar are all at extremes, and equities are at their lows.

Headline CPI is high, which fits 2008 (it peaked in July 2008 and then fell). A z-score of +2 for headline CPI with a 12m change of +2 suggests a year-over-year rate that is still elevated but may be falling. The 3m change of +1 suggests CPI is still rising, so this is probably not after October.

The unemployment z-score is +3, but the unemployment rate in late 2008 was only around 6.5%, and the 36-month window of 2005–2008 included lows near 4.4%. That could give a z-score of about +3 by November or December 2008.

The fed funds rate at -2 reflects cuts to 1% in October 2008 and 0-0.25% in December. The 2-year yield at -2 and the 10-year at -2 are also consistent with that. Payrolls at -2 and industrial production at -2.5 fit as well.

The 10y-2y spread at +2 and VIX at +3 with a 3m change of +3 suggest a recent spike. Investment-grade credit at -3 for 1m fits October 2008, when it fell sharply. Treasuries 7-10y at -0.5 over 1m fits that month too, since Treasuries were weak in October. Gold at +0.5 for 1m is plausible.

The 3m headline CPI change of +1 is odd for October, since CPI in October was falling month on month, but the 3m change in the year-over-year rate from July to October is plausibly still positive in z-score terms. The 3m dollar change of +2.5 fits the rally from July to October.

The unemployment 3m change of +2 and the 12m change of +2.5 fit October 2008 as well (6.5% against 4.7% a year earlier). I choose October 2008.
